transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling extremely depressed, sad, and completely empty inside lately. These struggles have been going on for about a year and a half now, and it has just become too difficult to handle on my own.
During this year and a half, have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or needed much less sleep than normal?

No, I've never had periods like that at all. I've mostly just felt completely drained and exhausted, never energetic or talkative. I definitely haven't had times where I felt like I needed less sleep.
Over the past year and a half, have you felt this way nearly every single day, or have there been periods of a few months or more where you felt like your usual self?

I haven't had any periods where I felt back to my usual self; it has been a constant struggle for the whole year and a half. Even when the deep sadness lifts slightly, the strange thoughts and experiences are still there, so I never really get a break. It feels like I've been dealing with one or both of these issues the entire time.
You mentioned having 'strange thoughts and experiences' even when the sadness lifts; could you describe what those experiences are like?

It often feels like there are people watching me and monitoring my every move, even when I'm just alone in my room. I also hear whispering voices calling my name or talking about me when there is no one else around. These things happen even during the times when I don't feel quite as down or depressed.
Have you ever experienced these voices or the feeling of being watched during a time when you were not feeling depressed at all, for a period of two weeks or longer?

Yes, I have. There was a period of about three weeks a few months ago where my mood felt completely normal and I wasn't feeling depressed at all, but the voices and the feeling of being watched were still happening every day. It made me realize that those experiences don't just go away when my mood gets better.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports experiencing psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusions of being watched) for a period of at least two weeks in the absence of a major mood episode. This fulfills the diagnostic criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, making Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features unlikely, as the latter requires psychotic symptoms to occur exclusively during a mood episode.
